**Clinical Note Template**

**1. Patient Information**

Name: Arthur Miller
Age/Gender: 80/Male
Hospital Stay Dates: October 26, 2023 to November 15, 2023 (with multiple discharges and readmissions)
Admitting Diagnosis:  Metastatic Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases, Acute-on-Chronic Pain, and Urinary Retention
Discharge Diagnosis: Metastatic Prostate Cancer with Bone Metastases,  Partial Spinal Cord Compression (L3-L4),  Sepsis (resolved),  Urinary Tract Infection (resolved)


**2. Visit Details**

**[October 26, 2023, 14:30]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Intractable back pain, urinary retention, increasing weakness.
Interventions:  Physical examination, urinalysis, complete blood count (CBC), basic metabolic panel (BMP), prostate-specific antigen (PSA) level,  chest x-ray,  CT scan of the lumbar spine.
Findings/Results:  Urinalysis showed pyuria and bacteriuria. CBC revealed leukocytosis (WBC 15,000/µL). BMP showed elevated creatinine (1.8 mg/dL). PSA level was 120 ng/mL.  Chest x-ray was unremarkable. CT scan of the lumbar spine revealed metastatic lesions at L3-L4 with significant spinal canal stenosis causing partial cord compression.
Treatment Plan:  Admitted to hospital.  Placement of indwelling urinary catheter.  Initiated intravenous antibiotics (Cefazolin 1g IV q8h) for presumed urinary tract infection.  Ordered analgesics (Morphine Sulfate 2mg IV q2h PRN for pain).  Consult with Oncology and Neurosurgery.


**[October 27, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Assessment of metastatic prostate cancer and treatment plan.
Interventions: Review of imaging studies, discussion of treatment options with patient and family.
Findings/Results: Confirmed metastatic prostate cancer with significant bone involvement.  Partial spinal cord compression noted.
Treatment Plan:  Recommended palliative radiotherapy to the L3-L4 vertebrae to reduce spinal cord compression.  Continued intravenous analgesics and antibiotics.  Discussed options for hormone therapy and bisphosphonates.


**[October 29, 2023, 10:00]**

Provider Role: Neurosurgeon
Reason for Visit:  Pre-operative assessment for radiotherapy.
Interventions:  Neurological examination.
Findings/Results:  Patient exhibits mild lower extremity weakness and decreased sensation.  Surgical intervention deemed not immediately necessary given the response to analgesics.
Treatment Plan:  Approved radiotherapy plan.


**[October 30, 2023, 15:00]**

Provider Role: Radiation Oncologist
Reason for Visit:  Initiation of radiotherapy.
Interventions:  External beam radiotherapy to L3-L4 vertebrae commenced.
Findings/Results:  Patient tolerated procedure well.


**[November 2, 2023, 11:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Follow-up on pain management and infection.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of labs.
Findings/Results:  Pain improved following radiotherapy.  Urinary tract infection resolved (negative urine culture).  Leukocytosis resolved.  Continued mild lower extremity weakness.
Treatment Plan:  Continued morphine sulfate for pain management (transition to oral morphine).  Discharged home with home health nursing for pain management and wound care.


**[November 10, 2023, 16:00]**

Provider Role: Emergency Physician
Reason for Visit:  Sudden onset fever, chills, and increased pain.
Interventions:  Physical examination, CBC, BMP, blood cultures, chest x-ray.
Findings/Results:  Elevated temperature (102°F), increased WBC count (18,000/µL),  positive blood cultures (Staphylococcus aureus).  Chest x-ray showed new right lower lobe infiltrate.
Treatment Plan:  Readmitted to the hospital.  Started intravenous antibiotics (Vancomycin and Piperacillin-Tazobactam).


**[November 12, 2023, 09:00]**

Provider Role: Infectious Disease Specialist
Reason for Visit:  Consultation for sepsis.
Interventions:  Review of cultures and clinical picture.
Findings/Results:  Confirmed sepsis secondary to Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia.
Treatment Plan:  Continued broad-spectrum antibiotics.


**[November 14, 2023, 14:00]**

Provider Role: Attending Physician
Reason for Visit:  Assessment of response to antibiotics.
Interventions:  Physical examination, review of labs and cultures.
Findings/Results:  Improved clinical status; fever resolved, WBC count decreasing.  Blood cultures now negative.
Treatment Plan:  Continued antibiotics for 24 hours and then transitioned to oral antibiotics.  Discussed palliative care options with patient and family.


**3. Key Events During Hospitalization**

*   **Radiotherapy:**  External beam radiotherapy to L3-L4 vertebrae from October 30, 2023, resulting in significant pain reduction.
*   **Sepsis:**  Developed sepsis secondary to Staphylococcus aureus pneumonia on November 10, 2023, successfully treated with intravenous antibiotics.
*   **Significant Diagnostic Findings:**  Metastatic prostate cancer with bone metastases and partial spinal cord compression.


**4. Ongoing Management and Care**

Throughout the hospitalization, Mr. Miller received intravenous and then oral analgesics for pain management, intravenous and oral antibiotics for the treatment of urinary tract infection and sepsis, and radiotherapy for spinal cord compression.  He received regular nursing care, including wound care and monitoring of vital signs.  Consultations with Oncology, Neurosurgery, and Infectious Disease were obtained.


**5. Discharge Summary**

Discharge Medications:  Oral Morphine Sulfate 10mg q4h PRN for pain,  Oral Cefixime 400mg once daily for 7 days.
Follow-up Instructions:  Follow-up appointment with oncologist in one week.  Home health nursing visits scheduled three times per week for pain management and wound care.  Palliative care referral.
Prognosis:  Poor prognosis due to advanced metastatic prostate cancer.  Focus on palliative care to manage symptoms and improve quality of life.
